concepts.title: Shivaji and the Foundation of the Maratha Empire
concepts.definition: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj laid the foundation of the Maratha Empire in the 17th century by uniting the Maratha hill chiefs and establishing an independent kingdom rooted in the Deccan.
concepts.key_idea: Shivaji built a disciplined army, captured key forts, and introduced a system of administration that combined local Deccan traditions with innovations in revenue, military, and governance.
question_patterns: Who founded the Maratha Empire and in which region?
Name two forts captured by Shivaji.
Explain the significance of Shivaji's coronation in 1674.
How did Shivaji unite the Maratha hill chiefs?
What was the role of the Mavlas in Shivaji's army?

solution_steps.explain: Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire in the Deccan region.
Capture of forts like Torna, Raigad, and Sinhagad established his power base.
The 1674 coronation formalized the independent Hindu kingdom of the Marathas.

worked_examples.question: Who founded the Maratha Empire and where?
worked_examples.solution: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in the Deccan region of India.

worked_examples.question: Why was Shivaji's coronation in 1674 significant?
worked_examples.solution: It formally declared the Maratha state as an independent Hindu kingdom and legitimized Shivaji as Chhatrapati.
worked_examples.answer: It established the Maratha Empire as an independent kingdom.

worked_examples.question: Name two famous forts associated with Shivaji.
worked_examples.solution: Raigad and Sinhagad are two prominent forts linked with Shivaji.

exercises.question: Describe the early life of Shivaji and his rise to power.
Which fort did Shivaji capture first?
The coronation of Shivaji took place in which year?

concepts.title: Maratha Administration: Ashtapradhan
concepts.definition: The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers appointed by Shivaji to assist in governance, covering areas such as finance, military, justice, and foreign affairs.
concepts.key_idea: The Ashtapradhan system provided a structured administrative framework where each minister had a defined portfolio, ensuring efficient governance of the Maratha state.
question_patterns: What was the Ashtapradhan?
Name any three members of the Ashtapradhan.
What was the role of the Peshwa in the Ashtapradhan?
How did the Ashtapradhan help in administration?
Who headed the Ashtapradhan council?

solution_steps.explain: It was a council of eight ministers assisting the king in administration.
Peshwa (finance/general), Amatya (finance), Sachiv (correspondence), Mantri (chronicler).
It ensured division of work and efficient governance of the Maratha state.

worked_examples.question: What was the Ashtapradhan?
worked_examples.solution: The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers appointed by Shivaji to manage different aspects of administration.

worked_examples.question: Who was the head of the Ashtapradhan?
worked_examples.solution: The Chhatrapati (king) headed the Ashtapradhan, with the Peshwa as the principal minister.
worked_examples.answer: The Chhatrapati, assisted by the Peshwa.

exercises.question: Explain the functions of the Ashtapradhan.
Name three portfolios under the Ashtapradhan.

concepts.title: Maratha Military System
concepts.definition: The Maratha military system comprised infantry, cavalry, and a strong navy, with guerrilla warfare tactics (Ganimi Kava) being a distinctive feature.
concepts.key_idea: Shivaji organized a disciplined standing army paid by the state, relied on light cavalry and guerrilla tactics, and built a navy to protect the coast.
question_patterns: What was Ganimi Kava?
Describe the structure of the Maratha army.
Why did Shivaji build a navy?
What role did the cavalry play in Maratha warfare?
How were soldiers paid in the Maratha army?

solution_steps.explain: The army had infantry, cavalry, and a navy with soldiers paid directly by the state.
Guerrilla warfare tactics used surprise, mobility, and terrain knowledge to defeat larger armies.
The navy protected the Konkan coast and secured maritime trade routes.

worked_examples.question: What was Ganimi Kava?
worked_examples.solution: Ganimi Kava referred to the guerrilla warfare tactics used by the Marathas to outmaneuver larger enemy forces.
worked_examples.answer: Guerrilla warfare tactics of the Marathas.

worked_examples.question: Why did Shivaji build a navy?
worked_examples.solution: To protect the Konkan coast from foreign navies like the Portuguese, Siddis, and British, and to secure trade.
worked_examples.answer: To protect the coastline and secure maritime trade.

exercises.question: The Maratha army was paid by the state. True or False?

concepts.title: The Peshwas and Their Role
concepts.definition: The Peshwas were the prime ministers of the Maratha Empire who, after the death of Shivaji, gradually became the de facto rulers and led the expansion of the empire.
concepts.key_idea: Bajirao I and Balaji Baji Rao were notable Peshwas who expanded Maratha influence across northern and central India, transforming the empire into a major pan-Indian power.
question_patterns: Who were the Peshwas?
Name two famous Peshwas.
What was the role of Bajirao I?
How did the Peshwas change the Maratha Empire?
Where was the Peshwa capital located?

solution_steps.explain: The Peshwa was the prime minister who administered the empire on behalf of the Chhatrapati.
Balaji Vishwanath, Bajirao I, and Balaji Baji Rao expanded Maratha power.
Over time the Peshwa at Pune became the de facto head of the Maratha state.

worked_examples.question: Who were the Peshwas?
worked_examples.solution: The Peshwas were hereditary prime ministers of the Maratha Empire who became the real executive heads.
worked_examples.answer: Prime ministers and de facto rulers of the Maratha Empire.

worked_examples.question: Name two famous Peshwas.
worked_examples.solution: Bajirao I and Balaji Baji Rao were two famous Peshwas.

exercises.question: Explain the rise of the Peshwas in the Maratha Empire.

concepts.title: Expansion of the Maratha Empire
concepts.definition: Under the Peshwas, the Maratha Empire expanded from the Deccan to large parts of northern, central, and eastern India, creating a vast but loosely held territory.
concepts.key_idea: Maratha expansion brought them into conflict with regional powers and the Mughals, but the rapid expansion also weakened central control over distant territories.
question_patterns: Which regions did the Marathas expand into?
Who led the Maratha expansion into North India?
What were the consequences of rapid Maratha expansion?
How far did the Maratha influence extend at its peak?
Why did expansion weaken central Maratha control?

solution_steps.explain: Marathas expanded into Malwa, Gujarat, Bundelkhand, Punjab, and Bengal regions.
Bajirao I and his generals like Holkar, Scindia, and Gaekwad led the expansion.
Rapid expansion stretched resources and weakened central control over distant provinces.

worked_examples.question: Which regions did the Marathas expand into?
worked_examples.solution: The Marathas expanded into Malwa, Gujarat, Bundelkhand, Punjab, and parts of Bengal and Orissa.
worked_examples.answer: Malwa, Gujarat, Bundelkhand, Punjab, Bengal, Orissa

worked_examples.question: Who led the Maratha expansion into North India?
worked_examples.solution: Bajirao I led the Maratha expansion into North India.

exercises.question: Discuss the expansion of the Maratha Empire under the Peshwas.
Name two regions conquered by the Marathas.

concepts.title: Maratha Confederacy
concepts.definition: The Maratha Confederacy was a decentralized political structure where powerful Maratha chiefs like the Holkars, Scindias, Gaekwads, and Bhonsles operated semi-independently under the nominal authority of the Peshwa.
concepts.key_idea: The confederacy allowed regional Maratha chiefs to govern their territories independently, which both expanded Maratha influence and weakened central unity over time.
question_patterns: What was the Maratha Confederacy?
Name the main Maratha chiefs of the confederacy.
How was the confederacy different from a centralized empire?
What was the role of the Peshwa in the confederacy?
Why did the confederacy weaken the Marathas?

solution_steps.explain: It was a union of semi-independent Maratha chiefs under the nominal Peshwa authority.
Holkars (Indore), Scindias (Gwalior), Gaekwads (Baroda), Bhonsles (Nagpur).
Lack of central unity led to internal rivalries and vulnerability to external enemies.

worked_examples.question: What was the Maratha Confederacy?
worked_examples.solution: The Maratha Confederacy was a decentralized system where powerful Maratha chiefs ruled semi-independently under the Peshwa's nominal leadership.
worked_examples.answer: A decentralized union of Maratha chiefs.

worked_examples.question: Name the main Maratha chiefs of the confederacy.
worked_examples.solution: The Holkars, Scindias, Gaekwads, and Bhonsles were the main Maratha chiefs.

exercises.question: Explain the structure of the Maratha Confederacy.
Why did the confederacy weaken the Marathas?

concepts.title: Conflict with Mughals and Afghans
concepts.definition: The Marathas fought prolonged conflicts with the Mughal Empire and later the Afghans, culminating in the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, a major defeat for the Marathas.
concepts.key_idea: Maratha conflicts with the Mughals weakened both empires, while the defeat at Panipat against Ahmad Shah Abdali halted Maratha expansion in the north for a generation.
question_patterns: Describe the Maratha conflict with the Mughals.
What happened at the Third Battle of Panipat?
Who was Ahmad Shah Abdali?
Why was the Third Battle of Panipat significant?
What was the impact of Panipat on the Marathas?

solution_steps.explain: Marathas fought Mughal armies under Aurangzeb for decades in the Deccan, draining Mughal resources.

solution_steps.action: Explain the Third Battle of Panipat
solution_steps.explain: In 1761, the Marathas were defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat.
The defeat halted Maratha northward expansion and weakened the confederacy temporarily.

worked_examples.question: What happened at the Third Battle of Panipat?
worked_examples.solution: In 1761, the Marathas were defeated by the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali at the Third Battle of Panipat.
worked_examples.answer: Maratha defeat by Ahmad Shah Abdali in 1761.

worked_examples.question: Who was Ahmad Shah Abdali?
worked_examples.solution: Ahmad Shah Abdali was the Afghan ruler who defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat.
worked_examples.answer: The Afghan ruler who defeated the Marathas at Panipat.

exercises.question: Explain the significance of the Third Battle of Panipat.
In which year was the Third Battle of Panipat fought?

concepts.title: Legacy of the Marathas
concepts.definition: The Marathas left a lasting legacy in administration, military organization, and resistance to foreign rule, and their regional states continued into the 19th century.
concepts.key_idea: The Maratha legacy includes contributions to guerrilla warfare, regional governance, and a tradition of resistance that influenced later Indian politics and the freedom movement.
question_patterns: What was the legacy of the Marathas?
How did the Marathas influence later Indian politics?
Name two Maratha states that survived into the 19th century.
What was the Maratha contribution to military strategy?
How did the Marathas resist foreign rule?

solution_steps.explain: The Marathas left systems of revenue collection and local governance used by successor states.
Guerrilla warfare and mobile cavalry tactics influenced later Indian military thinking.
Maratha states like Gwalior and Baroda survived until British annexation and shaped regional politics.

worked_examples.question: What was the legacy of the Marathas?
worked_examples.solution: The Marathas left a legacy in administration, military strategy, and resistance to foreign rule, with regional states surviving into the 19th century.
worked_examples.answer: Contributions to administration, military strategy, and resistance to foreign rule.

worked_examples.question: Name two Maratha states that survived into the 19th century.
worked_examples.solution: Gwalior (Scindias) and Baroda (Gaekwads) were two Maratha states that survived into the 19th century.

exercises.question: Discuss the legacy of the Marathas.
Name one Maratha contribution to military strategy.
